ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under Monetary and Financial Code Articles L.561-4-1 and L.561-10; mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and ultimate beneficial owners against the French national financial sanctions list maintained by Direction Générale du Trésor, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions lists, and TRACFIN typology indicators; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for all politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign) and their family members and close associates under Article L.561-10-2; OFAC SDN screening is required in practice by US-based payment processors such as Stripe and PayPal and should be included in the compliance protocol; screening must occur before incorporation and upon any UBO or directorship change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) maintained by INPI: https://data.inpi.fr; commercial registry data and name conflict searches also available via Infogreffe: https://www.infogreffe.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Constitutive documents and the published articles of association must be in French; company names may include foreign terms but must be written in Latin script; if the name originates in a non-Latin alphabet, the French registration filing must use an official or sworn transliteration into Latin characters; generic French descriptive terms and terms contrary to public policy are not permitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the chosen name is rejected at the registration filing stage, the applicant may contest the refusal before the registrar judge of the competent commercial court (juge commis chargé du registre) within 30 days from notification of the refusal; the appeal must be filed through the relevant Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE) or directly with the registry, accompanied by the refusal decision, a memorandum explaining why the name is distinctive and lawful, and evidence of the proposed corrected name; a further appeal against the judge's decision may be brought to the Cour d'appel within one month.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for an SAS carrying on online retail of automotive replacement parts and tuning accessories; the registered office may be located at the premises of a regulated commercial domiciliation company under Code de commerce Articles L.123-11-1 and R.123-137 et seq.; virtual office arrangements are lawful, but the domiciliation provider must be duly licensed/declared where required and the company must maintain adequate legal address facilities within France; banking and AML/KYC scrutiny may require additional proof of commercial substance and operational data.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low baseline risk of approximately 5-10% per year for a standards-compliant, low-risk online auto-parts retailer using an approved domiciliation address; the likelihood increases to approximately 20-25% if tax, VAT, customs, or payment-rail anomalies arise, and may exceed 35% if the company is selected for an administrative, tax, or TRACFIN examination.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce, articles L. 227-1 et seq. (Sociétés par actions simplifiées)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) du Tribunal de Commerce
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de constitution et statuts de la société
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement for SAS under French law; capital may be subscribed in cash or in kind
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The First Board Meeting of the newly incorporated SAS was convened to address the following: (1) Ratify the share subscription by the initial shareholders and confirm full payment of the share capital; (2) Adopt the registered office at the designated address; (3) Appoint the initial officers including the Président, Directeur, and other corporate officers; (4) Authorize the opening of corporate bank accounts and the execution of all necessary incorporation documents. All resolutions were passed unanimously by the board members.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Draft Statutes and Share Subscription Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of association detailing the corporate purpose, share capital, registered office, and management structure. Secure signatures from all shareholders on the share subscription agreements. Ensure compliance with French company law requirements.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity and address for shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, submit additional supporting documents or make amendments within 10 business days

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Filing with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public followed by submission to RCS via guichet-entreprises.fr or in person
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have the draft statutes notarized by a French notary. Submit the original act of incorporation, statutes, and payment receipt to the RCS of the relevant Tribunal de Commerce. The RCS will assign the SIREN and SIRET numbers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If incomplete, the filing may be refused and the applicant notified to provide missing documents within 15 days

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Incorporation in Legal Announcements
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice of incorporation in the official legal announcements journal. Obtain the publication certificate from the RCS. This completes the public registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is rejected, amend the notice and resubmit within the prescribed period

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE for SIRET, tax authorities, and other bodies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with INSEE for the SIRET number if not obtained. File for VAT number if applicable. Open corporate bank account and notify employees if any. Ensure compliance with labor and social security registrations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried by authorities, provide explanations and supporting documents promptly to avoid penalties

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No specific industrial licensing authority required for retail activities; general business registration suffices
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required; company registration with RCS serves as primary operating permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: French Environment and Energy Management Agency (ADEME) or local environmental services
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for retail and online sales activities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No manufacturing, production, or emissions; retail operations comply with general waste and pollution prevention standards

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Compliance with fire safety regulations, structural inspections for office premises, and workplace health and safety clearances as per Labor Code

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), France / French Tax Authority. VAT registration and filings are managed by the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) local tax office; corporate registrations occur through the Guichet Unique des Formalités (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); e-invoicing will be cleared through the French Public Billing Portal (PPF) and certified dematerialisation platforms (PDPs).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French-established SAS, incorporation via the Guichet Unique automatically generates the SIREN/SIRET business identifiers and the French intra-Community VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire) by INSEE and DGFiP. The SAS must subsequently register with the SIE for corporate income tax and VAT liabilities. For a non-resident entity performing taxable French supplies without a French permanent establishment, registration is effected by submitting form 1656 or the simplified VAT registration form to the local SIE, after appointing a tax representative when required for non-EU sellers; the authority issues a French VAT number (FR + 11 digits). Any cross-border goods operator must also obtain an EORI number (FR prefix) for customs/export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not employ a US-style check-the-box election. An SAS is subject to corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) by default at 25% for standard profits. However, a small SAS may opt for transparency and be taxed as an income-tax partnership (régime des sociétés de personnes under CGI Art. 239 bis D) provided it has fewer than 5 employees, turnover below €10,000,000, and satisfies shareholder eligibility conditions. An SAS can also elect to form a French VAT grouping under Article 257 C CGI, to join a fiscal consolidation regime for IS (intégration fiscale), and, for cross-border structures, must observe France's anti-hybrid mismatch rules (CGI Art. 212 bis) transposing ATAD – no elective hybrid mismatch exit is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business supplying goods such as automotive aftermarket parts, the franchise de base de TVA (VAT exemption threshold) is €85,000 of annual turnover for supplies of goods, with a tolerance band up to €93,500. Once turnover exceeds the €93,500 tolerance, VAT registration becomes mandatory. For intra-EU distance sales of goods, a pan-European €10,000 threshold applies for the EU OSS regime; above that, VAT registration is required in each destination Member State or via the Union OSS. Non-established foreign sellers making taxable French sales have no general EU turnover threshold and are required to register for French VAT from the first transaction in France unless an OSS/import regime applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has implemented a phased mandatory e-invoicing reform aligned with the E-invoice Directive. Real-time fiscal clearance is not yet active, but mandatory structured e-invoicing (Factur-X, UBL, CII) and electronic transmission (EDI) of transaction data are required through certified dematerialisation platforms (PDPs). For VAT purposes, the reform is effective from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-size taxpayers and from 1 September 2027 for small and micro enterprises. The tax administration receives invoice data through the Public Invoicing Portal (PPF); no physical stamping or real-time pre-clearance is required, though eligible PDPs must transmit automatically to the PPF.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies constituting an export to a destination outside the EU (CGI Art. 262 ter I) and to intra-Community dispatches (CGI Art. 262 ter II). For exports of goods, the seller must evidence the goods physically left France and the EU within the statutory timeframes (customs summary declarations and proof of departure). For intra-EU supplies, a valid EU VAT number of the acquirer, an EC Sales List, and the dispatch/transport evidence are required. Offshore services (including certain digital/e-commerce services) supplied to an economic operator located outside the EU are zero-rated under CGI Art. 259 A where the effective use and enjoyment of service are outside the EU. The taxpayer must retain contemporaneous evidence including contracts, payment documents, and certification of the customer's business status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Combined customs export declaration (Déclaration Unique d'Exportation / DAU) of the good leaving France/EU
International transport documentation: Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill, CMR consignment note, or postal export label
Commercial invoice issued by the exporting SAS
Inward remittance certificate / bank settlement attestation proving receipt of foreign currency or euros from the foreign buyer
Proof of the customer's overseas taxable status (VAT registration certificate or equivalent)
EC Sales List / Intrastat declaration for intra-Community dispatches, where applicable
EORI number and customs export movement identification (MRN) confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is examined strictly by DGFiP and Customs (DGDDI). Failure to substantiate the export within the legal periods triggers retrospective VAT assessment at the 20% standard rate, plus late-payment interest (0.20% per month) and penalties. Deliberate concealment or misuse of zero-rating may attract the 80% penalty under CGI Art. 1729, possible criminal liability for tax fraud under CGI Art. 1741 (up to 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of €75,000, or 500,000€ for organised fraud), plus a 5-year statutory limitation (10 years for hidden/fraudulent activity) and potential denial of refund claims. Directors of a French SAS may be held personally liable for fraudulent export filings.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) acting as the monetary and financial stability authority, with prudential supervision of credit institutions and electronic money institutions delegated to the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution); the Direction Générale du Trésor administers balance-of-payments statistics and investment controls under the Article 63 TFEU free-movement-of-capital framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a Eurozone member, maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility for all EUR transactions and for cross-border dealings with non-EU counterparties, subject only to EU financial sanctions and anti-money-laundering filters. Profit remittance of distributable reserves by the SAS to foreign shareholders is unrestricted, though dividend payments attract domestic withholding tax at 30% unless reduced under a DTT (e.g., US-France 0% or 15% under entitlement to benefits). No prior exchange-license authorization is required for online retail export proceeds or supplier payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No legal obligation to surrender, repatriate, or convert export proceeds exists because the EUR is the lawful currency of the receiving company; a French resident SAS may freely retain foreign currency balances. All cross-border payments routed through resident credit institutions are captured at the transactional level for the Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting (BASE-EC), with the intermediary bank acting as declarant; no affirmative filing by the SAS is required for individual export receipts below EUR 50,000, while larger flows are aggregated and reported by the PSP.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte Courant) with multicurrency sub-ledger
Operational Account + SécuriPass cash management overlay

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole CIB (via Caisses Régionales réseau)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for shareholder injection and ISD (ISDA) margin
Operational Account for trade settlements and FX forward execution
Operational Account (retail-grade, unsuitable for FX hedging)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for EUR collections and SEPA payouts through ACPR-licensed electronic money institutions (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Portland/4649-class passported EMIs) using PSD2 passporting; however, offshore EMIs incorporated outside the EEA (e.g., HK/US digital banks) are legally restricted from holding deposits on behalf of the SAS without a French banking license. Therefore a two-rail strategy is advised: (i) Stripe/PayPal aggregating card traffic into a tier-1 French operational account, and (ii) an EMI secondary account for SEPA disbursements, while rejecting USD-denominated incoming wires via EMI bridges because of sanctions and beneficiary-name mismatching risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted under L. 561-5-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code for French-resident legal representatives using a qualified electronic signature (eIDAS), but tier-1 French commercial banks nearly always impose an in-person interview at the bank branch for the SAS legal representative (président) when the UBO structure includes non-EU shareholders. For a fully digital SAS with a non-resident director, a pragmatic route is a hybrid procedure: remote identity verification via TRACFIN-approved video KYC followed by a single notarized apostilled resolution, or an introduction through a specialized corporate-services firm to secure a Paris-based corporate account within 3 to 5 weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Online-only business model with no physical trading premises and a registered office at a domiciliation service provider
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed co-working/office leasing agreement; detailed ISIC 4791 business plan with projected revenues; live dashboard of Marketplace Stripe/PayPal transaction volume; valid EU VAT number and customs EORI FR registration; supplier ECG-qualified purchase agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owners resident in high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., Hong Kong, UAE, or Turkey) with >25% shareholding quota in the SAS
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original passport copies plus apostilled certificates of good standing; tax-residence certificates from the relevant treaty jurisdiction; TRACFIN-compliant UBO register filing (art. L. 561-2-2); source-of-funds file covering the initial capital contribution; audited financial statements of the ultimate parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated chargeback ratios on DSM (Debit/Step Merchant) rails for automotive parts triggering suspicion of logistics-fraud typology
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chargeback report showing < 0.65% monthly ratio for the trailing quarter; 3-D Secure authentication logs; valid logistics track-and-trace evidence for each disputed sales order; documented CDP/CX dispute-resolution policy; AML transaction monitoring threshold calibrated to €10k per order.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Supplier disbursements to high-sanction-risk jurisdictions (China, Taiwan, Thailand, Singapore) for aftermarket parts inventory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Restricted-party screening results against EU Consolidated FS List, OFAC SDN crosswalk, and UN list; harmonized customs tariff codes (HS 8708, 8709, 8512, 8409) confirming non-dual-use classification; documentary LC or open-account contract with beneficial-owner declarations of the counterparty.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity subscription must be wired via SWIFT MT103 with reference 'APPORT CAPITAL SAS' and the Banque de France statistical purpose code 'FC-1' (equity participation), to the SAS dedicated capital escrow account; the notary drafts a deed of incorporation and confirms the deposit prior to registration. Shareholder loans to the SAS must be evidenced by a written loan agreement and transmitted via MT103 with purpose code 'LOAN' and the TRE-FS (economic interest) threshold rules: the French thin capitalization limitation under art. 212 C.G.I. restricting interest deductibility to 30% of EBITDA; all inbound non-EU funds are subjected to the bank's FX match-check between the payee name and the SAS registry to prevent sanctions flags.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to Chinese and EU auto-parts vendors will be cleared via SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 'GDS' (goods) and an explicit Customs EORI reference for each goods invoice; for bulk high-value inventory purchases exceeding USD 250,000, a documentary letter of credit (UCP600) with a 90-day usance tenor and a confirmed French issuing bank reduction of supplier-country risk is used. SEPA CT (Credit Transfer) rails are used for EU sub-30k EUR payments, while SEPA Direct Debit is avoided as the collection protocol for B2B dealer accounts; FX conversion is executed against the bank's auto-FX sweep from the EUR balance to USD payables at the closing spot mid-rate plus a capped 0.15% margin.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD forwards up to 24 months documented under a French-law ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with CSD margin posting
Plain-vanilla OTC EUR/USD currency swaps with legally centralized credit support annex (CSA) for existing non-EUR supplier liabilities
European-style EUR/USD FX options (call-and-put spreads) for the retail sales business, restricted to net exposure
Short-term EUR/USD rolling spot (TOM/NEXT contracts) for cash sweeps and receivable monetization

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible as standard ACPR-authorised instruments for EUR pairs under the free-convertibility regime; any NDF would require a separate ISDA NDF annex and is operationally disfavored.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (Comptes annuels) deposited with the commercial registry after shareholder approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registrar of the Commercial Court)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months of shareholder approval and in all cases within seven months of financial year end; calendar-year fiscal year entities must file by 30 July unless a court-approved extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Judicial injunction with coercive penalty payments (astreinte), fine up to €15,000 for the legal entity, possible criminal sanctions for directors, and administrative strike-off (radiation) after formal notice and continued default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Déclaration de résultats / liasse fiscale) including income tax computation and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of financial year close; calendar-year companies must file no later than 3 May of the following year (subject to harmonised deadlines for remote areas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of tax due, increased to 40% after 30 days, plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; enforcement measures may include tax enforcement and criminal penalties for habitual non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register update (Déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE) for any share transfers or ownership changes occurring during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via Infogreffe national platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven annual confirmatory obligation: filing due within 30 days of each qualifying share transfer or change in beneficial ownership; no separate recurring filing if no change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to €7,500 for the legal entity and €1,500 for natural persons, potential judicial corrective order, and prolonged default may trigger administrative enforcement compliance proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is required if the SAS exceeds at least two of the following at the end of the financial year: €4,000,000 balance sheet total, €8,000,000 net turnover, or 50 average employees; articles may impose a lower threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the Plan Comptable Général (PCG) applies to statutory individual accounts; IFRS is permitted only for consolidated financial statements of listed or certain subsidiaries.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under French law, there is no separate annual UBO re-filing. The beneficial owner declaration filed at the commercial registry must be updated within 30 days of each share transfer or change in beneficial control; the annual corporate maintenance process verifies that the RBE matches the share register and minutes for the preceding year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% for financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2022
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced CIT rate of 15% applied to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% held by individuals or equivalent). Research Tax Credit (CIR) up to 30%, Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20%, and partial CIT exemption for Young Innovative Enterprises (JEI) may apply.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (each year the offset is limited to 50% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1 million; the first EUR 1 million of taxable profit is always offsetable without restriction)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa N° 2065-SD (déclaration de résultats et d'impôt sur les sociétés) together with annexes 2051-SD to 2059-SD; electronic filing mandatory through the EFI-TDFC portal at www.impots.gouv.fr or via an EDI partner/competent accountant.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return must be filed by the second business day after 1 May, typically 2 or 3 May. For a non-calendar fiscal year, filing must occur within three months after the fiscal year-end. CIT instalments are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December; the balance is payable with the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: French business registration and establishment numbers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SAS with a French permanent establishment (PE) must use the SIREN/SIRET issued for that PE; do not enter foreign registration numbers in this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered company name, legal form, share capital, postal address and head office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the French branch address as well as the foreign parent company's name, legal form, registration country and registration number, where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selectable regime for corporation tax; SAS is always subject to IS unless an exemption applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SAS must tick the 'IS' box and state that it operates in France through a PE; treaty protection does not eliminate the filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net book profit or loss before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reported figure must be limited to the French PE's attributable book result under the French tax treaty definition and Article 209 I CGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result after fiscal reintegrations, deductions, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must compute French-source taxable income attributable solely to the French PE, applying transfer pricing adjustments for intercompany transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base subject to the standard 25% CIT rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities generally do not benefit from the 15% reduced rate unless they are French tax-resident under domestic criteria.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 – Base de l'IS à taux réduit (15%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of taxable profit eligible for the 15% SME reduced rate (maximum EUR 42,500).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete only if the non-resident is effectively a French-resident SME; otherwise leave blank.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Available tax loss carryforward brought forward from previous years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only prior-year losses of the same French PE may be deducted; foreign parent losses cannot be used against French PE profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 6 – Crédits d'impôt et retenues à la source subies
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal tax credits, foreign tax credits, CIR, CII and other prepaid credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report credits relating to French activities; foreign tax credits are unavailable unless a tax treaty authorizes them.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net corporate income tax due after application of credits and pre-payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the balance and the return are paid electronically by the statutory deadline; instalments already paid must be reconciled.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% uplift on the tax due after formal notice; 40% if the inaccuracy is in bad faith; 80% for deliberate tax evasion or participation in an abusive scheme. Late payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month (2.4% per annum). Failure to file entirely may lead to taxation d'office under Articles L.66 and L.67 LPF and suspension of payment deadlines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% on gross French-source dividends paid to non-residents under CGI Article 119 bis 2. A 0% rate applies under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive when the EU corporate shareholder holds 5% or more of the capital and has held it for at least 24 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply for DTA relief, the non-resident corporate shareholder must obtain a certificate of tax residence (Formulaire 5000, or 5001 if a request for reduced withholding is needed) certified by the foreign tax authority. The certificate must be provided to the French paying agent or the French tax centre before the distribution date. EU parent companies should file Form 5002 or provide equivalent proof of eligibility under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, including percentage of capital and two-year holding period. The payer must retain the documentation and may apply the reduced rate only after validation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents on French-source industrial/commercial intellectual property attract domestic withholding at 30%, often reduced or eliminated under DTAs (commonly 0% or 5%). Interest paid by a French borrower to a non-resident lender is not generally subject to French withholding unless paid to a non-cooperative state, in which case a 75% withholding applies. EU Interest-and-Royalties Directive exemption is available for related companies under conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 (net consolidated turnover excluding VAT, whether of the French head company or of the foreign parent group); a simplified documentation obligation applies to entities conducting cross-border transactions with related parties exceeding EUR 7,000,000 or transacting with entities located in tax havens.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no Economic Substance Regulation analogous to offshore ESR regimes. Nevertheless, the general anti-abuse doctrine (abus de droit, Article L.64 LPF) and the EU ATAD anti-abuse provisions deny tax treaty or directive benefits to structures lacking real economic substance. An SAS or non-resident PE must demonstrate actual business premises, employees, common governance, and substantive decisions made in France. Artificial ownership and profit allocation without operational substance will be recharacterized, with penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting French PE or SAS taxable income, concealing online auto-parts sales from French enforcement authorities, using fictitious invoices, failing to register for CIT in France while carrying on a complete commercial activity through a French website/delivery network.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud under Article 1741 CGI is punishable for natural persons by up to 5 years' imprisonment and a EUR 75,000 fine; aggravated fraud can raise the sanction to 7 years' imprisonment and EUR 250,000 fine. The tax administration may apply a deliberate-failure penalty of 40% or a fraud penalty of 80% on the reassessed tax, plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president of an SAS may be held personally liable under Article L.267 LPF for tax debts caused by fraudulent manoeuvres or repeated failures to pay. A criminal conviction may result in imprisonment, personal fines, commercial management bans, and a travel ban preventing the director from leaving French or EU territory.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing auto-parts imports or ecommerce services from related foreign suppliers/manufacturers at inflated transfer prices, or understating French PE profits by allocating excessive royalties, management fees, or interest to a foreign parent company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the French taxable base to the arm's length result plus sanctions: 10% penalty if the omission is simple, 40% in bad faith, 80% for tax fraud, applied with 0.20% monthly late-payment interest. France also applies a 5% penalty on the amount of hidden distributions or profits painstakingly disguised intercompany transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign manipulated filings or direct intercompany invoicing policy may be subject to personal tax liability under L.267 LPF and could be joint and severally liable for penalties where fraudulent acts are demonstrated. Criminal liability under Article 1741 also extends to active directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement (Abus de Droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming or maintaining an SAS merely as a mailbox entity without staff or premises, or routing ecommerce profits through a nominally French intermediary to claim DTA benefits or VAT registration advantages; arrangement has no genuine economic reality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article L.64 LPF permits the tax authority to ignore the artificial transaction and tax the underlying economic reality. The taxpayer faces a 80% penalty for abus de droit in addition to reassessed tax and late-payment interest. Companies using abusive cross-border arrangements may also incur a penalty of 10% of the arranged amount under Article 1729(6) CGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director may be made personally liable for the resulting tax debt under Article L.267 LPF if the arrangement is an intentional sham. Criminal prosecution for fraud is possible, with imprisonment, fine, prohibition on managing a company, and a travel ban as potential ancillary measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Disclose Beneficial Ownership / AML Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file with the French Trade and Companies Registry (RCS) the identity of the beneficial owners of the SAS within 15 days of registration, or intentionally obscure the ultimate ownership when opening Stripe/PayPal merchant accounts or payment processing routes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-disclosure of beneficial owner information is punishable by a fine of up to EUR 15,000, and for legal persons up to EUR 75,000. Failure to register a commercial business (immatriculation au RCS) may result in rejection of the corporate tax return and legal standing issues. Payment intermediaries may freeze funds and report suspicious activity to TRACFIN.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly provide false beneficial ownership information may be held personally liable for fines and are exposed to criminal sanctions for false certificates. Personal assets can be attached after repeated non-compliance; travel bans and imprisonment can follow where AML notification violations accompany tax fraud.
